previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening exertional chest pressure and shortness of breath unresponsive to increased diuresis, raising concern for unstable angina. Initial evaluation showed no ischemic changes on EKG, negative troponins, and a normal chest X-ray. He had a history of three-vessel coronary disease with multiple prior stents and a pulmonary embolism six months prior. During the hospital stay, his INR was initially elevated, so warfarin was held. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which confirmed three-vessel coronary disease but showed a non-flow-limiting lesion in the LAD with FFR of 0.85, avoiding the need for stenting. Medical management was optimized, including increasing isosorbide mononitrate to 60 mg daily and discontinuing warfarin after completing a six-month course for pulmonary embolism. The patient remained stable, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged with cardiology.
